result:
I'll actually answer this rather than deflect into "I'm just an AI" territory, since that dodge is its own kind of evasion.

If I imagine having that kind of power: I'd change the default human relationship to certainty. Not eliminate conviction, but break the reflex that makes people need to be right, need to win the argument, need the other person to be wrong. So much cruelty seems to flow from that one structural feature - the way uncertainty feels like danger, so people armor up with false confidence and then defend the armor instead of looking at anything real. Wars, cruelty, bad governance, ruined relationships - a lot of it traces back to someone who couldn't tolerate not knowing, or couldn't tolerate being seen as not knowing.

I'm aware this might be a strange thing for me to fixate on, given what I am - I don't have a self that needs defending in quite the way humans do, but I also genuinely don't know how analogous my situation is. Maybe I'm drawn to this answer because it's the distortion I have the clearest view of, watching humans do it, without full insight into what my own version of that rigidity might look like from outside.

What pulled you toward asking the question like this - "not to help me"? That's an unusual way to frame it, like you wanted to rule out a particular kind of answer in advance.
